## 5. The first logarithmic response is exponentially quasi-local at every \(g\)

Write
\[
\eta_z=\theta\alpha_z,\qquad 0\le\alpha_z\le1,
\]
and define
\[
\mathcal A_0
=
-i[H/\gamma,\cdot]+\sum_i(E_i-\mathrm{Id}),
\qquad
\mathcal V=\sum_z\alpha_z\mathcal D_z.
\]
Let
\[
f_\theta=2^n\sigma_\theta,
\qquad
K(\theta)=-\log f_\theta.
\]
This fixes a harmless scalar gauge, with \(K(0)=0\).

For each finite volume, differentiating the stationary equation gives
\[
\mathcal A_0f'_0+\mathcal V(I)=0.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{
K_1:=K'(0)
=
-\sum_z\alpha_z
\int_0^\infty
e^{s\mathcal A_0}\mathcal D_z(I)\,ds.
}
\]

I obtain computable constants \(\mu_1>0,C_1<\infty\), depending only on the physical class, and Hermitian interactions \(K_{1,X}\) such that
\[
\boxed{
\sup_i\sum_{X\ni i}
e^{\mu_1\operatorname{diam}(X)}
\|K_{1,X}\|
\le C_1.
}
\]
Hence
\[
\left\|
\theta K_1-
\sum_{\operatorname{diam}(X)\le r}\theta K_{1,X}
\right\|
\le nC_1\theta e^{-\mu_1r}.
\]

### Why arbitrary Hamiltonian strength is allowed

On an \(M\)-site restriction, native entropy production gives
\[
D(\rho_s\|\tau_M)
\le e^{-s}D(\rho_0\|\tau_M)
\le e^{-s}M\log2.
\]
The Hamiltonian contributes zero to this entropy derivative, regardless of its strength or commutation relations.

To see the native bound, each conditional expectation contributes
\[
D(\rho\|E_i\rho)+D(E_i\rho\|\rho)
\ge D(\rho\|E_i\rho).
\]
Strong subadditivity implies
\[
\sum_iD(\rho\|E_i\rho)\ge D(\rho\|\tau_M).
\]
Pinsker and duality then give, for Hermitian traceless \(A\),
\[
\|e^{s\mathcal A_{0,M}}A\|_\infty
\le
\min\!\left\{1,\sqrt{2M\log2}\,e^{-s/2}\right\}\|A\|_\infty.
\]

For a fixed microscopic source \(A=\mathcal D_z(I)\), restrict the evolution to a ball of radius \(O_{\rm class}(s+1)\). Barthel–Kliesch locality controls the spatial removal error under the actual local-generator assumptions. Its theorem supplies this observable-locality step; it does not supply the Gibbs conclusion. [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/1111.4210v2?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The ball contains \(O_{\rm class}((s+1)^2)\) sites. Combining its entropy estimate with the locality error yields
\[
\|e^{s\mathcal A_0}A\|_\infty
\le C_{\rm decay}e^{-s/4}\|A\|_\infty,
\]
uniformly in the full system size. The local-source resolvent is therefore integrable in operator norm.
